question: The Bumchu festival is primarily celebrated in which of the following states of India?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Sikkim.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Bumchu festival is primarily celebrated in the state of Sikkim, which is located in the northeastern part of India.**
 
• This festival is celebrated at the** Tashiding Monastery, considered one of the most sacred monasteries in Sikkim.**
 
• The festival is celebrated on the **15th day of the first Tibetan month,** usually in February or March.
 
• The festival's main highlight is the unveiling of the sacred pot of water, which is believed to predict the region's future for the coming year.
 
• Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh do not celebrate the Bumchu festival.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himachal Pradesh** is known for its various festivals, such as the **Kullu Dussehra, Chamba Minjar Mela, and Shimla Summer Festival.**
 
• **Maharashtra **is known for its Ganesh Chaturthi festival, which is celebrated with** great enthusiasm and devotion.**
 
• ** Andhra Pradesh** is known for its Ugadi festival, which marks the beginning of the** Telugu New Year.**
